questions.q: What does the course say to do with the root user after creating the account?
options: Use it only to create your first IAM user, then stop using it for daily work
questions.explain: The root user cannot be restricted by any policy, so a leak gives full control of the account and bill.

questions.q: When is the secret access key shown?
options: Only once, at creation, so save it in a password manager
questions.explain: Create the key with the CLI use case and store it safely.

questions.q: Why attach AdministratorAccess to your own IAM user in this lesson?
options: It is required by the CLI
It is your day-to-day login, not a service credential; least privilege for service roles comes later
questions.explain: The policy is broad on purpose for this personal user.

questions.q: Which two beginner mistakes does the module aim to prevent?
options: Using MFA, and using the CLI
Using too many regions, and using IAM
Using the root user day-to-day, and not understanding regions/profiles
questions.explain: Confusion about regions and profiles causes 'where did my resource go?' bugs.

questions.q: Which IAM identity uses temporary credentials and is assumed by users or AWS services?
questions.explain: There is no long-lived secret to leak.

questions.q: Why attach policies to a group rather than to each user?
options: You manage permissions for a team without repeating yourself
questions.explain: Add users to the group and they inherit its policies.

questions.q: What are the parts of a policy statement?
questions.explain: The example grants read-only access to exactly one bucket.

questions.q: Is IAM region-scoped?
questions.explain: It's the most important service to understand before provisioning anything else.

questions.q: What is an AMI?
options: A template of OS and pre-installed software an instance boots from
questions.explain: The instance type is the hardware profile, such as t3.micro.

questions.q: Why chmod 400 the .pem private key?
options: SSH refuses a private key file that other users could read
questions.explain: AWS cannot give the private key back, so losing it means creating a new key pair.

questions.q: What does it mean that security groups are stateful?
options: A response to an allowed inbound request is automatically allowed back out
questions.explain: You rarely need explicit outbound rules for typical request/response traffic.

questions.q: Why allow SSH only from your own IP /32 rather than 0.0.0.0/0?
options: It's safer: only your address can attempt to connect
questions.explain: HTTP on port 80 from anywhere is the web-server exception in the lesson.

questions.q: What must be true of an S3 bucket name?
options: Globally unique across all of AWS
questions.explain: Not just unique in your own account.

questions.q: What does aws s3 sync do?
options: Uploads only changed or new files from a directory
questions.explain: It's the efficient way to push a whole local directory.

questions.q: What does enabling versioning do?
options: Keeps every version of an object instead of overwriting, at the cost of storing (and billing) each version
questions.explain: It protects against accidental deletes and overwrites.

questions.q: When do you use aws s3api instead of aws s3?
options: For lower-level operations like bucket policies and versioning configuration
questions.explain: aws s3 is the friendly high-level command set.

questions.q: What makes a subnet public?
options: It is in a big CIDR
It has a route to an Internet Gateway
questions.explain: Resources there can have public IPs; private subnets have no direct route to the internet.

questions.q: What does a NAT Gateway allow?
options: Private-subnet resources to make outbound internet calls without being reachable from outside
questions.explain: It's used for databases and internal services that need to reach out.

questions.q: Why did Module 3's EC2 instance work without networking setup?
options: It landed in the default VPC, pre-wired with public subnets
questions.explain: New accounts get a default VPC in every region.

questions.q: A /16 VPC CIDR provides how many addresses?
questions.explain: A /24 subnet provides 256.

questions.q: What does RDS handle for you?
questions.explain: You focus on schema and queries instead of database administration.

questions.q: Why does RDS require a DB subnet group with two subnets in different AZs?
options: It requires at least two AZs even for a single-AZ instance
questions.explain: The lesson creates a second private subnet in us-east-1b.

questions.q: What does --source-group do in the database security group rule?
options: Allows traffic from anything in the app security group instead of specific IPs
questions.explain: It's the standard 'app tier talks to data tier' pattern.

questions.q: What is the trade-off of RDS versus installing a database on EC2 yourself?
options: Less low-level control: you can't SSH into the underlying OS
questions.explain: In exchange you get automatic backups with point-in-time recovery, patching and Multi-AZ failover.

questions.q: What do you pay for in Lambda?
options: The milliseconds your code actually executes
questions.explain: It scales from zero to thousands of concurrent invocations.

questions.q: What determines what a Lambda function can access?
options: Its execution role, not the caller's identity
questions.explain: The role is assumed by the Lambda service via a trust policy.

questions.q: What is a cold start?
options: The latency of provisioning a fresh execution environment for the first invocation or after scaling up
questions.explain: It's one of the core Lambda concepts.

questions.q: What is the bare minimum policy every Lambda function needs?
questions.explain: Add more permissions only as the function actually needs them.

questions.q: What are CloudWatch namespaces?
options: Groups of metrics such as AWS/Lambda, AWS/EC2 and AWS/RDS
questions.explain: Every AWS service publishes metrics grouped into namespaces.

questions.q: Where does Lambda's print()/logging output land?
options: A CloudWatch log group /aws/lambda/<function-name>, created automatically
questions.explain: No setup is required on your part.

questions.q: Which command tails a Lambda's most recent log events live?
questions.explain: It's great for live-debugging.

questions.q: What does a CloudWatch alarm do?
options: Notifies you when a metric crosses a threshold
questions.explain: The module sets one up alongside reading metrics and logs.

questions.q: What is the difference between a CloudFormation template and a stack?
options: A template is the YAML/JSON description; a stack is the running set of resources created from it
A template is a running instance
questions.explain: CloudFormation tracks the stack's resources together so it can update or delete them as a unit.

questions.q: What does 'drift' mean in the IaC table?
options: Console clicks that change resources invisibly; diffing against the template reveals them
questions.explain: Manual changes are invisible without an IaC record.

questions.q: How do you tear down everything a template created?
options: Delete each resource ID by hand
One command deletes the stack and its resources
questions.explain: Manual teardown means remembering every resource.

questions.q: What does !Ref BucketName do in the template?
options: Inserts the value of the BucketName parameter
questions.explain: Parameters make templates reusable across environments.

questions.q: What are the pieces of the capstone's architecture?
options: S3 static site, API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB
questions.explain: It's a notes app where visitors add and read notes.

questions.q: Why PAY_PER_REQUEST billing for the DynamoDB table?
options: It charges only for reads/writes actually made, with no capacity to provision, right for low traffic
questions.explain: On-demand billing is the right default for a training app.

questions.q: Why does the lesson stress the Teardown section?
options: Free tier is free below a usage threshold, and only 12 months on some resources, so leftover resources can bill you
questions.explain: Tear down every time you finish working, not just at the end of the course.

questions.q: How does DynamoDB compare with RDS conceptually?
options: Both are managed with no server to patch, but DynamoDB is key-value/document shaped rather than relational
questions.explain: It's new in this module but parallel to Module 6.

questions.q: What does the Fargate launch type remove?
options: Provisioning and patching the underlying EC2 instances
questions.explain: You specify vCPU and memory per task and AWS handles the host.

questions.q: What is a task definition?
options: A JSON blueprint of images, CPU/memory, ports, roles and logging
questions.explain: A task is a running instance of it.

questions.q: What does an ECS service do?
options: Keeps a desired number of tasks running, replacing any that die
questions.explain: It can also register tasks with a load balancer.

questions.q: Why do CI pipelines re-authenticate to ECR each run?
options: The get-login-password token is valid for 12 hours
ECR forbids caching in all cases
questions.explain: They don't cache the token.

questions.q: What does an Auto Scaling Group do?
options: Keeps a fleet of identical instances running, replaces failed ones and scales with demand
questions.explain: It maintains the fleet between min/max size.

questions.q: What does an ALB health check do?
options: Probes targets, and failing ones stop receiving traffic
questions.explain: It's defined on the target group.

questions.q: Why must UserData be base64-encoded in the JSON launch-template example?
options: The CLI does not encode it for you when embedded in a JSON string
questions.explain: Each instance runs the script once at boot.

questions.q: What is a launch template?
options: A reusable blueprint of AMI, instance type, security groups and user data
questions.explain: The ASG creates instances from it.

questions.q: Why use an alias record rather than a CNAME for a zone apex?
options: CNAMEs are not allowed at all
Alias records work at the zone apex and point at AWS resources like an ALB, CloudFront or S3 website
Aliases need a TTL of zero
questions.explain: It's a Route 53-specific record type.

questions.q: What is a hosted zone?
options: A container for DNS records for one domain, with its own 4 name servers
questions.explain: For a real subdomain you'd add those name servers as NS records at your registrar.

questions.q: What does TTL control?
options: How long resolvers cache a record before re-querying
questions.explain: Time-to-live.

questions.q: What is --caller-reference for?
options: A unique value per call so retried requests aren't treated as duplicates
questions.explain: A timestamp works.

questions.q: How do SNS and SQS differ?
options: SNS is a queue; SQS is pub/sub
SNS is pub/sub fan-out to many subscribers; SQS is a queue where each message is processed by one consumer
questions.explain: Combining SNS → multiple SQS queues is the fan-out pattern.

questions.q: What does the visibility timeout do?
options: Hides a received-but-not-deleted message from other consumers to avoid double-processing
questions.explain: The lesson sets it to 30 seconds.

questions.q: What does maxReceiveCount: 5 mean?
options: A message received and left unprocessed 5 times moves to the dead-letter queue
questions.explain: The DLQ stops failing messages blocking the queue forever.

questions.q: How does a FIFO queue differ from a standard queue?
options: Ordered, exactly-once processing (.fifo suffix) versus at-least-once, best-effort order
questions.explain: Standard queues are the default.

questions.q: What does a composite key of customerId (partition) + orderId (sort) enable?
options: Fetching all orders for one customer in a single efficient query
questions.explain: Items sharing a partition key are stored together and range-queryable by sort key.

questions.q: What is a GSI?
options: An alternate partition/sort key over the same table, queryable independently with its own eventually-consistent copy
questions.explain: It's the main tool for querying by something other than the primary key.

questions.q: How does an LSI differ from a GSI?
options: Uses the same partition key with an alternate sort key, created only at table creation, supporting strongly consistent reads
questions.explain: From the lesson's concept table.

questions.q: When is PROVISIONED capacity cheaper than on-demand?
questions.explain: PAY_PER_REQUEST charges per read/write; PROVISIONED reserves RCU/WCU.

questions.q: What does Elastic Beanstalk do?
options: Provisions and manages EC2, ASG, ALB and security groups from a single application upload
questions.explain: You deploy code; Beanstalk manages the servers, while still allowing access to the underlying resources.

questions.q: What is an application version?
options: One uploaded, deployable build (a zip in S3) with a kept history
questions.explain: An environment runs one version.

questions.q: What are .ebextensions?
options: Config files in your bundle that customize the environment's resources
questions.explain: They can add packages, config and resources.

questions.q: What do the web server and worker environment tiers do?
options: Web handles HTTP traffic; worker processes an SQS queue in the background
questions.explain: Choose per environment.

questions.q: Why avoid putting a database password in a Lambda environment variable?
options: It's visible to anyone with read access to the function configuration and never rotates
questions.explain: Use Secrets Manager or Parameter Store instead.

questions.q: What does Secrets Manager offer that plain Parameter Store focuses less on?
questions.explain: Rotation is done via a Lambda function on a schedule.

questions.q: What does get-secret-value return by default?
questions.explain: Every write creates a new version, and prior versions remain retrievable.

questions.q: What does a SecureString parameter use?
questions.explain: String and StringList are plain.

questions.q: What does CloudFront do?
options: Caches content at edge locations so repeat requests are served near the visitor
questions.explain: It also provides managed HTTPS in front of an S3 bucket.

questions.q: What does Origin Access Control (OAC) allow?
options: CloudFront to authenticate to a private S3 bucket so the bucket stays non-public
questions.explain: This is the CloudFront-recommended pattern, unlike the Level 1 public bucket policy.

questions.q: What is an invalidation?
options: A request to purge specific paths from edge caches before the TTL expires
questions.explain: It's used when content changes before the cache would naturally refresh.

questions.q: What is a cache behavior?
options: Per-path-pattern rules: origin, what varies the cache key, and TTLs
questions.explain: It lives inside the distribution configuration.

questions.q: What does an AWS Budget do when the threshold is crossed?
options: Only notifies, unless you wire it to an automated action
questions.explain: Crossing 100% does not stop anything from running or accruing cost.

questions.q: What is Cost Explorer?
options: A queryable view of historical spend, groupable by service, tag or account
questions.explain: It also provides forecasts.

questions.q: What does a cost allocation tag enable?
options: Attributing spend to a project, team or environment in billing reports
questions.explain: For example Project=training, activated for billing.

questions.q: What is the Cost and Usage Report?
options: The most granular billing export, one row per line item, dumped to S3
questions.explain: It's a CSV or Parquet dump.

questions.q: How does the Level 2 project differ from the Level 1 capstone?
options: Containerized, load-balanced and globally distributed rather than serverless
questions.explain: It uses ECS/Fargate, ALB, DynamoDB, Route 53 and CloudFront.

questions.q: How does the API reach DynamoDB without credentials?
options: An access key in the image
questions.explain: Secrets Manager would only hold third-party API keys.

questions.q: What serves the static frontend?
options: CloudFront in front of a private S3 bucket via OAC
questions.explain: It's cached at the edge.

questions.q: What does the byRecency GSI support?
options: Querying recent notes across all users
questions.explain: The base key is userId + noteId.

questions.q: What does it mean that VPC peering is non-transitive?
options: If A peers with B and B with C, A cannot reach C through B
questions.explain: Each pair needs its own connection.

questions.q: After accepting a peering connection, what else is required?
options: Route table entries on each side and security groups allowing the traffic
questions.explain: Accepting isn't enough.

questions.q: Why use Transit Gateway instead of full-mesh peering?
options: Peering grows O(n²) (10 VPCs need 45 connections); TGW is hub-and-spoke with one attachment per VPC
questions.explain: TGW also supports multicast and cross-region peering.

questions.q: What must be true of VPC CIDR ranges to connect them?
questions.explain: Peering and Transit Gateway cannot route between colliding ranges.

questions.q: When should you choose EKS over ECS?
options: For multi-cloud portability, existing Kubernetes expertise or ecosystem tools that assume Kubernetes APIs
questions.explain: ECS has a lower learning curve but is AWS-only.

questions.q: How is the EKS control plane billed?
options: A flat hourly rate per cluster regardless of size, plus your worker compute
questions.explain: It also takes 10–15 minutes to provision.

questions.q: What does kubectl authentication rely on after update-kubeconfig?
options: aws eks get-token, so it fails if your AWS CLI credentials expire
questions.explain: No long-lived credentials are stored in ~/.kube/config.

questions.q: What does a managed node group handle?
questions.explain: For serverless pods, use Fargate profiles instead.

questions.q: Why use Step Functions instead of chaining Lambdas in code?
options: The flow, retries and error handling become a visible first-class resource, not buried in code
questions.explain: It also doesn't bill compute while waiting.

questions.q: What language defines a state machine?
options: Amazon States Language (ASL), a JSON dialect
questions.explain: The example defines ValidateOrder → IsValid → ProcessPayment → ShipOrder.

questions.q: What do Retry and Catch provide?
options: Per-state exponential backoff and error branching without try/except code
questions.explain: For example IntervalSeconds 2, MaxAttempts 3, BackoffRate 2.0.

questions.q: What does the Choice state do?
options: Branches on a condition, e.g. $.valid being true, with a Default branch
questions.explain: Invalid orders go to RejectOrder.

questions.q: What can a Service Control Policy do?
options: Set a ceiling on what an account or OU can do; it never grants permissions
questions.explain: A user with AdministratorAccess still can't do what an SCP denies.

questions.q: What does a permission boundary cap?
options: The maximum permissions of an individual role or user, even if admin policies are attached
questions.explain: It lets teams create roles without privilege escalation.

questions.q: Effective permissions are the ____ of the attached policy and the boundary.
questions.explain: AdministratorAccess on a bounded role is still capped at S3, Lambda and Logs.

questions.q: What does NotAction with Deny in the region SCP do?
options: Denies everything except a short list of global services, outside the approved regions
questions.explain: Common pattern for region lockdown.

questions.q: Which Terraform command previews changes before applying them?
questions.explain: It is the equivalent of CloudFormation change sets; always read it before apply.

questions.q: What is the biggest conceptual shift from CloudFormation?
options: Terraform uses an explicit .tfstate file that you own
questions.explain: Losing or corrupting it leads to Terraform and AWS disagreeing about what exists.

questions.q: Why store state remotely (S3 with DynamoDB locking) in production?
options: Local state breaks when two people apply at once
questions.explain: Locking prevents concurrent applies.

questions.q: How does Terraform differ from CloudFormation in rollback on failure?
options: Terraform has no built-in rollback (manual), CloudFormation rolls back automatically
questions.explain: From the comparison table.

questions.q: What are the roles of CodePipeline, CodeBuild and CodeDeploy?
questions.explain: Together they form AWS's native pipeline.

questions.q: Where does CodeBuild read its commands from?
questions.explain: It has install, pre_build, build and post_build phases.

questions.q: Why tag images with the commit SHA (CODEBUILD_RESOLVED_SOURCE_VERSION) instead of latest?
options: It makes rollbacks to a specific prior build possible
questions.explain: CodeBuild injects that variable automatically.

questions.q: What stages does the example pipeline move an artifact through?
questions.explain: CodePipeline defines the stages.

questions.q: What is RTO?
options: How long you can tolerate being down
How much data you can lose
questions.explain: RPO is how much data you can tolerate losing.

questions.q: Which DR strategy keeps only the database running in the DR region with compute scaled to zero?
questions.explain: On failover you promote the replica and scale up compute.

questions.q: Which is the cheapest strategy and what is its RTO?
options: Backup & Restore, with hours of RTO
questions.explain: Nothing runs in the DR region until a declared disaster.

questions.q: How should you pick a DR strategy?
options: Work backward from business requirements, not default to the most expensive
questions.explain: Costs rise with faster recovery.

questions.q: What does X-Ray provide that per-resource logs don't?
options: Distributed tracing: one trace ID follows a request across every service it touches
questions.explain: Segments sharing a trace ID are stitched into one trace shown as a service map.

questions.q: What does Mode=PassThrough do on Lambda?
options: Traces only if the incoming request already carries a trace header
questions.explain: Mode=Active traces invocations subject to the sampling rule.

questions.q: What does patch_all() do?
options: Auto-instruments libraries such as boto3 and requests so calls appear as subsegments
questions.explain: A DynamoDB get_item shows up with its own latency.

questions.q: What does filter-expression 'service("validateOrder") { fault }' find?
options: Traces where that service raised an error
questions.explain: You can also filter by response time, status or annotations.

questions.q: What does GuardDuty analyze?
options: VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and CloudTrail events against threat intelligence and anomaly models, with no agents to install
questions.explain: Findings are scored 1–10 by severity.

questions.q: How does WAF differ from a security group?
options: WAF inspects HTTP request content (SQLi patterns, rate limits, geo blocks); security groups filter by IP/port
questions.explain: WAF attaches to CloudFront, ALB or API Gateway.

questions.q: What does Security Hub provide?
questions.explain: It aggregates findings from services like GuardDuty.

questions.q: How can high-severity GuardDuty findings trigger automated response?
options: Route them to EventBridge with a rule on severity
questions.explain: The example matches severity >= 7.

questions.q: Why does the project promote the same image from staging to prod by SHA tag?
options: The exact image tested in staging is what is promoted, never a rebuild
questions.explain: Two clusters share one ECR repository.

questions.q: What does the Manual Approval stage do?
options: A human approves in the console or CLI before Deploy-Prod
questions.explain: It sits between Deploy-Staging and Deploy-Prod.

questions.q: What does least privilege mean for the CodeBuild role here?
options: It can push to ECR, write logs and read source, but cannot call ecs:UpdateService
questions.explain: Each role gets only what its stage needs.

questions.q: How is production deployed in the pipeline?
questions.explain: Deploy-Prod targets the prod cluster.

questions.q: How many pillars does the Well-Architected Framework have?
questions.explain: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization and Sustainability.

questions.q: Which pillar asks 'Are you spending money only where it delivers value?'
questions.explain: Each pillar has a core question.

questions.q: What does a Well-Architected review make you do about trade-offs?
options: State them deliberately rather than by accident
questions.explain: Higher reliability usually costs more.

questions.q: What do unanswered questions surface as?
options: Risks, flagged as High or Medium Risk Issues
questions.explain: The lens review report summarizes high and medium risks per pillar.

questions.q: Why create custom event buses per domain?
options: So application events don't mix with AWS service events, and cross-account access can be scoped per bus
questions.explain: The default bus receives AWS service events.

questions.q: What does put-permission allow?
options: Another AWS account to publish to your bus without sharing credentials
questions.explain: The shipping account uses its own IAM role.

questions.q: What does content-based pattern matching on detail.tier achieve?
options: priorityFulfillment fires only for enterprise orders with no tier check in code
questions.explain: The filtering happens at the bus level.

questions.q: What does the schema registry offer?
options: Inferred schemas and generated typed code bindings, turning field knowledge from tribal to explicit
questions.explain: For example OrderPlaced schemas for consumers.

questions.q: What is the data lake pattern in this lesson?
options: Raw data in S3, described by the Glue Data Catalog and queried in place by Athena
questions.explain: No data movement and no cluster to manage for ad-hoc queries.

questions.q: Why partition S3 data by folders like year=2026/month=08/?
options: Query engines skip irrelevant partitions, which cuts cost since Athena bills per byte scanned
questions.explain: Columnar compressed formats such as Parquet help too.

questions.q: What does a Glue crawler do?
options: Infers schema and partitions from the S3 layout and registers a table in the Data Catalog
questions.explain: Athena, Redshift Spectrum and EMR can all use the same catalog entry.

questions.q: How is Athena billed?
questions.explain: It has no persistent infrastructure to provision.

questions.q: How does Karpenter differ from Cluster Autoscaler?
options: It provisions right-sized nodes directly for pending pods without ASGs, within seconds
questions.explain: It can mix spot and on-demand and consolidates underutilized nodes.

questions.q: What does a Karpenter NodePool define?
options: What kinds of nodes it's allowed to launch, e.g. instance categories and capacity types, with limits
questions.explain: The example allows c, m and r categories on spot or on-demand.

questions.q: What does GitOps with Argo CD mean?
options: The cluster continuously reconciles from a Git repo instead of kubectl apply from a laptop
questions.explain: The Application points at a repoURL, revision and path.

questions.q: What do managed node groups do that self-managed ones don't?
options: Handle draining and rolling updates for you
questions.explain: Self-managed gives full control but requires reimplementing that lifecycle.

questions.q: Why use multiple AWS accounts?
options: Hard blast-radius boundaries: billing, quotas and IAM are already account-scoped
questions.explain: One team's mistake can't affect another's production.

questions.q: What does Control Tower automate?
options: The landing zone: log archive and audit accounts, baseline SCPs and an Account Factory for compliant new accounts
questions.explain: New accounts are compliant from creation.

questions.q: What is the difference between detective and preventive guardrails?
options: Detective flags non-compliant resources via Config rules; preventive blocks actions outright via SCPs
questions.explain: Control Tower enforces both.

questions.q: Which is a typical OU?
questions.explain: Each OU carries its own SCPs.

questions.q: Which commitment is the most flexible?
options: Compute Savings Plans, applying across EC2, Fargate and Lambda
questions.explain: They give a slightly lower discount than instance-family-locked options.

questions.q: What do Spot Instances offer and risk?
options: The largest discount, but they can be reclaimed
questions.explain: Use them for interruption-tolerant workloads.

questions.q: What does capacityOptimized allocation pick?
options: Spot pools with the deepest available capacity (lowest interruption risk) rather than the cheapest price
questions.explain: Mixing several instance types widens the pool.

questions.q: What does get-savings-plans-purchase-recommendation do?
options: Analyzes recent usage and recommends a commitment level that covers steady state without over-committing
questions.explain: It looks back 30 or 60 days.

questions.q: How does Direct Connect differ from a VPN?
options: A dedicated physical connection that bypasses the public internet; a VPN still traverses it
questions.explain: VPN has variable latency and shared bandwidth.

questions.q: Why does Direct Connect provisioning take days to weeks?
options: It is physical: a provider uses AWS's Letter of Authorization to cross-connect at the location
questions.explain: Unlike every other resource in the path.

questions.q: What does a public VIF reach?
options: AWS public service endpoints such as S3 and DynamoDB over the dedicated link
questions.explain: A private VIF connects to a VPC; a transit VIF to a Direct Connect gateway.

questions.q: What is the production practice for Direct Connect resiliency?
options: Keep a Site-to-Site VPN as backup, failing over via BGP route priority
questions.explain: The highest resiliency is separate connections at two locations with diverse providers.

questions.q: What does AWS Config do?
options: Records every resource's configuration and changes and evaluates them against rules
questions.explain: A NON_COMPLIANT finding shows which resource drifted and when.

questions.q: How can Config rules be evaluated?
options: On change (near-real-time) or on a periodic schedule
questions.explain: Unlike a point-in-time manual audit.

questions.q: What is the lesson's advice on auto-remediation?
options: Good for well-understood low-risk fixes; test with Automatic: false first and review before auto-apply
questions.explain: It could disrupt legitimate configurations.

questions.q: How does compliance differ from threat detection?
options: Compliance verifies resources stay configured as policy requires and produces audit evidence
questions.explain: Examples: encryption enabled, no public S3 buckets.

questions.q: What is chaos engineering?
options: Deliberately injecting failures in a controlled way to see if the design survives them
questions.explain: It's better than finding out in a real outage.

questions.q: What makes FIS experiments safe on real infrastructure?
options: stopConditions, such as a CloudWatch alarm that halts the experiment
questions.explain: FIS halts if the high-error-rate alarm fires.

questions.q: Which action simulates a network partition between AZs?
questions.explain: It directly tests multi-AZ reliability claims.

questions.q: What does PERCENT(50) selectionMode do in the template?
options: Targets half of the matching tagged instances
questions.explain: The resourceTags select staging training-app instances.

questions.q: What goes in the log-archive account?
options: Org CloudTrail and the Config aggregator
questions.explain: It sits in the Security OU.
